question: Will Gemini 4 Argon be released publicly before October 15
resolution_criteria:
Resolution criteria

This market resolves to YES if Google makes its Gemini 4 Argon model publicly available to individual developers or consumers on or before October 14, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. Otherwise, this market resolves to NO.

To qualify as publicly available, ordinary individual users must be able to obtain access without being individually selected, invited, vetted, or approved by Google. Qualified access pathways include:

Developer Access: Available via Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, or Google Cloud Vertex AI for any registered developer.

Consumer Access: Offered via a generally available consumer subscription (e.g., Google AI Advanced, Google AI Ultra, or a successor tier) on the Gemini web or mobile interface.

Exclusions and Edge Cases:

Access does not qualify if it remains restricted to enterprise customers, select companies, private-preview cohorts, trusted testers, or members of specific closed initiatives such as Google's Fairwind program.

Paid subscriptions or paid API usage qualify as public access, as long as any ordinary user can sign up and pay.

Geographic restrictions will not prevent a YES resolution, provided ordinary individual users in at least one supported region can obtain unvetted access.

The model must be functionally accessible and interactive by the deadline; a mere announcement of a future release date does not suffice.

Background

Google announced its next-generation frontier AI model, Gemini 4 Argon, on September 30, 2026. Engineered for complex reasoning, multi-step software engineering (scoring 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1), and defensive cybersecurity, the model boasts a massive 1-million-token output capacity.

At launch, Google made Gemini 4 Argon available exclusively to trusted testers and select cybersecurity partners through its vetted Fairwind program. This market tracks whether Google transitions the model from its restricted early-access phase to general public availability for developers or consumers before the October 15, 2026 deadline.

I'm writing up the report now. I could only use search snippets, because every attempt to open a page failed at the proxy. Several results described events after 2026-10-03, so I left them out, as the exercise rules require.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria don't name a single URL. What decides it is whether Gemini 4 Argon can actually be used through Google AI Studio, the Gemini API or Vertex AI by any registered developer, or in the Gemini app on a consumer plan (AI Pro or Ultra). The pages to watch are the [Gemini API model page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-4-argon), the [Gemini app release notes](https://gemini.google/release-notes/), the [Vertex Model Garden listing](https://console.cloud.google.com/agent-platform/publishers/google/model-garden/gemini-4-argon) and the [Fairwind Program page](https://deepmind.google/fairwind-program/).
- I couldn't load any of these pages, so I can't confirm what they showed on or before 2026-10-03.

## 2. Current status (as of 2026-10-03)
- 2026-09-30: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Argon as "initially available to a set of trusted testers through our Fairwind Program." [X post](https://x.com/GoogleDeepMind/status/2105388084154056939), [Google blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-argon/)
- 2026-09-30/10-01: Coverage described access as "for trusted testers only." [Threads](https://www.threads.com/@poseidanai/post/Dd8N_ELjERQ/googles-gemini-argon-is-here-for-trusted-testers-only-up-to-m-output-tokens/)
- So far as I can find, nothing before the cutoff settles the question. On 2026-10-03 the model is still restricted to vetted access, which doesn't count under the criteria.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About 2026-10-01: The Hacker News reported Google was rolling Argon out to trusted cyber defenders and also planned a version without cyber guardrails for trusted defenders and internal teams. I couldn't open the article to check its exact date or whether it gave a timeline for public release. [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/google-rolls-out-gemini-4-argon-to.html)
- 2026-09-30: Google's headline claims were 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1, up to 1M output tokens, and "our most resilient model yet against indirect prompt injections." [Google blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-argon/)
- Pricing: secondary sources report an introductory API price of $2 input / $10 output per million tokens, later rising to $4 / $20. Listing a price hints at a planned API launch, but I couldn't date these figures to before the cutoff. [NeuralTrust](https://neuraltrust.ai/blog/gemini-4-argon), [Vals AI](https://www.vals.ai/models/google_gemini-4-argon)
- Fairwind rules: applicant organizations get background checks, must use phishing-resistant MFA, and access is limited to internal security teams. [WorkOS](https://workos.com/blog/gemini-4-argon-fairwind-access-control), [Let's Data Science](https://letsdatascience.com/news/google-releases-gemini-4-argon-to-cyber-defenders-1093bb0b)
- I couldn't find any official pre-cutoff statement such as "available to developers in the coming weeks." I also couldn't confirm whether the 2026-09-30 blog post gave a date for wider release.

## 4. Base rates
- 2026-09-02 to 09-03: Fairwind launched with Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, given exclusively to government agencies, critical-infrastructure operators and maintainers. Reports said broader access "remains limited," and I found no public release in the following month. [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/google-introduces-fairwind-programme-to-strengthen-cyber-defence-with-gemini-3-8-flash-cyber-553040-2026-09-03), [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/google-ships-gemini-38-flash-cyber-to-trusted-defenders-via-new-fairwind-program)
- That model was a specialized cyber variant. Argon is Google's general flagship and comes with published API pricing and a model ID (`gemini-4-argon`), so it may not follow the same path. Earlier Gemini flagships usually reached AI Studio or the Gemini app on announcement day, or as an experimental or preview release within days to a few weeks. This is the first frontier Gemini launched only to vetted testers, so there's no direct precedent.
- Comparable case: Anthropic and OpenAI have also held back cyber-capable frontier models for vetted partners first. In those cases the gap before public release has varied from weeks to open-ended.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market specifically on Argon reaching the public by Oct 15.
- Older general Gemini 4 markets exist, such as a Polymarket "Gemini 4.0 Flash publicly available by…" ladder (an earlier snapshot showed 8% for Sep 15 and 88% for Nov 30) and several Manifold "Gemini 4 release date" markets. Their criteria differ and the prices I found are stale. [next.io](https://next.io/prediction-markets/trending/when-will-gemini-4-0-be-released/), [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/gemini-40-google-release-date)

## 6. Upcoming events before 2026-10-14
- Watch for:
  - a Gemini API changelog or AI Studio entry for `gemini-4-argon`
  - a Gemini app release-note entry for Pro or Ultra subscribers
  - Vertex AI moving from private to public preview
- The planned guardrail-free version for defenders points to tiered access. A general version with safeguards could be released separately.
- I couldn't confirm any scheduled Google event (such as a developer conference or Cloud event) between Oct 3 and Oct 14.

Sources: [Gemini API docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-4-argon), [Google blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-argon/), [DeepMind X](https://x.com/GoogleDeepMind/status/2105388084154056939), [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/google-rolls-out-gemini-4-argon-to.html), [Threads](https://www.threads.com/@poseidanai/post/Dd8N_ELjERQ/googles-gemini-argon-is-here-for-trusted-testers-only-up-to-m-output-tokens/), [Fairwind](https://deepmind.google/fairwind-program/), [WorkOS](https://workos.com/blog/gemini-4-argon-fairwind-access-control), [Let's Data Science](https://letsdatascience.com/news/google-releases-gemini-4-argon-to-cyber-defenders-1093bb0b), [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/google-introduces-fairwind-programme-to-strengthen-cyber-defence-with-gemini-3-8-flash-cyber-553040-2026-09-03), [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/google-ships-gemini-38-flash-cyber-to-trusted-defenders-via-new-fairwind-program), [NeuralTrust](https://neuraltrust.ai/blog/gemini-4-argon), [Vals AI](https://www.vals.ai/models/google_gemini-4-argon), [next.io](https://next.io/prediction-markets/trending/when-will-gemini-4-0-be-released/), [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/gemini-40-google-release-date), [Gemini release notes](https://gemini.google/release-notes/)
